strategy.bottleneck: Per-call CPU launch/dispatch overhead: 11 kernel launches plus 12 torch::empty scratch allocations per forward, many micro-kernels (gstats_final 4.99us, 0.07 waves/SM, 3.43% occupancy) whose cost is pure launch latency; wall time exceeds summed kernel time.
strategy.optimisation method: Capture the whole fused_block launch sequence (wt_kernel, nchw2nhwc, 2x conv_gemm, 2x gstats_partial/final, norm_silu, final_epilogue) once per input shape into a torch.cuda.CUDAGraph over static input/output buffers, then replay it, eliminating per-call launch and allocator overhead.
strategy.modification plan:
1. Keep all CUDA kernel code, launch shapes and block sizes in _CUDA_SRC exactly unchanged; all edits are in ModelNew (Python).
2. In ModelNew.__init__, add `self._graphs = {}` (dict keyed by a capture key) and nothing else; the module stays stateless w.r.t. parameters.
3. Define the capture key as `(tuple(x.shape), x.dtype, x.device.index, tuple(conv1_weight.shape), float(eps))` so each of the four benchmark shapes (8x256x64x128, 2x256x64x64, 4x256x256x256, 1x256x131x131) and any eps change gets its own graph; never re-capture for a key already present.
4. Fallback guard at the top of forward: if `self.training or not x.is_cuda or torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()`, call `self._ext.fused_block(...)` directly and return — no graph path.
5. On a key miss, build static buffers with fixed addresses: `sx = torch.empty_like(x).contiguous()` and one `torch.empty_like` per weight/bias argument (conv1_weight, norm1_weight, norm1_bias, conv2_weight, norm2_weight, norm2_bias). Copy the current call's tensors into them with `.copy_()` before warmup so the warmup sees valid data.
6. Warmup: on a dedicated side stream `s = torch.cuda.Stream(); s.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())`, run `self._ext.fused_block(sx, ...)` 3 times inside `with torch.cuda.stream(s):`, then `torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(s)` and `torch.cuda.synchronize()`. This forces module load, JIT-resident code, and steady-state caching-allocator blocks for the internal scratch tensors before capture.
7. Capture: `g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()`; `with torch.cuda.graph(g):  out = self._ext.fused_block(sx, sw1, sg1, sb1, sw2, sg2, sb2, float(eps))`. The internal `torch::empty` scratch allocations (xn, y1, y2, wt1, wt2, psum, psq, mean/rstd) are legal inside capture: the caching allocator routes them to the graph-private pool and their addresses are frozen. Do NOT give an explicit shared `pool=` argument — each shape gets its own private pool so replays of different shapes can interleave safely.
8. Store `self._graphs[key] = (g, sx, [sw1,sg1,sb1,sw2,sg2,sb2], out)` where `out` is the tensor returned by the captured call (its address is now static).
9. Replay path (hit): `sx.copy_(x)` and one `.copy_()` per weight tensor (these are the only per-call H2D-free device copies; ~1MB weights + activation copy), then `g.replay()`.
10. Return `out.clone()` so a caller holding results from several rounds never sees them mutated by a later replay; the clone is one extra kernel (~16MB traffic, ~10us) versus a ~4.9ms forward.
11. Do not call `.cuda()`, `.cpu()`, or `.to(...)` anywhere; all static buffers are created with `torch.empty_like`, inheriting device and dtype from the incoming tensors.
12. Guard `x = x.contiguous()` and each weight `.contiguous()` before `.copy_()` so the captured pointer layout assumption in fused_block (which itself calls `.contiguous()`) can never trigger a fresh allocation on the replay path.
13. Cap graph count: if `len(self._graphs) > 8`, fall back to the direct extension call instead of capturing another graph, so memory never grows unbounded on unseen shapes.

strategy.modification plan:
1. Keep every __global__ kernel body, block size and grid computation in _CUDA_SRC byte-identical; all changes are in the C++ orchestrator `fused_block` plus a new persistent cache.
2. Add a file-static `struct Ctx { torch::Tensor xn,y1,y2,wt1,wt2,psum,psq,mean1,rstd1,mean2,rstd2; cudaGraphExec_t exec=nullptr; cudaGraph_t graph=nullptr; }` and `static std::map<std::tuple<int,int,int,int,float>,Ctx> g_cache;` keyed by (B,C,H,W,eps). Cap the map at 8 entries; beyond that use the plain eager path.
3. On a cache miss, allocate ALL scratch tensors exactly once with the current sizes (identical shapes to today: xn[M,C], y1/y2[Mpad,C], wt1/wt2[C*9,C], psum/psq[B*G*nchunk], mean/rstd[B*G]) and store them in the Ctx so their device addresses are frozen for the lifetime of the process.
4. Split the launch sequence into OUTSIDE-graph and INSIDE-graph parts. OUTSIDE (launched normally every call, because they touch caller-owned pointers): wt_kernel(w1->wt1), wt_kernel(w2->wt2), nchw2nhwc(xc->xn), final_epilogue(y2, xc, g2, b2, mean2, rstd2 -> out). INSIDE the graph (all operands are Ctx-owned, addresses fixed): conv_gemm_kernel(xn,wt1,y1), gstats_partial+gstats_final on y1, norm_silu(y1), conv_gemm_kernel(y1,wt2,y2), gstats_partial+gstats_final on y2. Note wt1/wt2/xn are written outside but read inside — legal, since only their addresses must be stable.
5. Warmup before capture: run the 7 inner kernels once eagerly on the current stream and `cudaStreamSynchronize`, so module load and any lazy driver work is done before capture.
6. Capture: create a dedicated `cudaStream_t cap` once; `cudaStreamBeginCapture(cap, cudaStreamCaptureModeThreadLocal)`; launch the 7 inner kernels on `cap` with exactly the same grid/block/shared-mem arguments used today; `cudaStreamEndCapture(cap,&graph)`; `cudaGraphInstantiate(&exec,graph,nullptr,nullptr,0)`. Perform NO torch::empty, no allocation and no ATen call between Begin/EndCapture.
7. Replay path (cache hit): launch wt_kernel x2 and nchw2nhwc on the current stream, then `cudaGraphLaunch(exec, at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream())`, then launch final_epilogue on the same stream, then return `out`. The replay path must contain zero `.copy_()`, zero clone, zero allocation other than the fresh `out = torch::empty_like(xc)`.
8. Guard: if `cudaStreamIsCapturing(current stream)` reports active capture, or `cudaGraphInstantiate` returns an error, fall back to the existing eager launch sequence using the same Ctx scratch buffers (correctness identical).
9. Keep `nchunk` derived exactly as today so gstats grid dims baked into the graph match the buffers allocated in step 3; eps and count are compile-time-constant per cache key, which is why eps is part of the key.
10. Do not add `.to()`, `.cuda()`, `.cpu()` anywhere; scratch is allocated with `xc.options()`.
11. Verify launch reduction: nsys should show 4 host launches + 1 graph launch per forward instead of 11.

strategy.modification plan:
1. Keep the explicit-graph + persistent per-(B,C,H,W,eps) Ctx scratch and the single cudaGraphLaunch per forward (the mechanism the base already carries). All scratch shapes unchanged.

Because HW % 128 == 0 the row range [b0*HW, b1*HW) is exactly (b1-b0)*HW/BM conv blocks, so chunks never share a BM tile. For the awkward shape (B=1, HW=17161) S=1 → today's structure, bit-identical.
4. Per-chunk node launch shapes/offsets (all other kernels keep their bodies): nchw2nhwc grid (HW+31)/32 x (C+31)/32 x (b1-b0) with src = x + (long)b0*C*HW, dst = xn + (long)b0*HW*C; conv_gemm grid dim3((b1-b0)*HW/BM, C/BN), 256 thr, 29696 B, base A/Y pointers, mbase = b0*HW/BM; gstats_partial grid dim3(nchunk,G,b1-b0), 128 thr, boff=b0, base psum/psq; gstats_final grid (b1-b0)*G, 32 thr, with psum/psq offset by (long)b0*G*nchunk and mean/rstd offset by b0*G; norm_silu grid ((nvec4_chunk+255)/256) with y + (long)b0*HW*C, mean/rstd + b0*G, nvec4 = (long)(b1-b0)*HW*C/4; final_epilogue grid dim3((HW+31)/32,(C+31)/32,b1-b0) with y2 + (long)b0*HW*C, xres = x + (long)b0*C*HW, out + (long)b0*C*HW, mean/rstd + b0*G.
5. DAG: two shared roots n_wt1, n_wt2 (no parents). For each chunk k build the chain t_k(nchw2nhwc, deps {}), c1_k(deps {t_k, n_wt1}), p1_k(deps {c1_k}), f1_k, ns_k, c2_k(deps {ns_k, n_wt2}), p2_k, f2_k, e_k(deps {f2_k}). No cross-chunk edges — chunks are provably disjoint in xn/y1/y2 rows, psum/psq (indexed (b*G+g)*nchunk+chunk), mean/rstd (b*G+g) and out.
6. Instantiate once per key with cudaGraphInstantiateWithFlags after one eager warmup of the same node sequence; store node handles + cudaKernelNodeParams + arg storage inside Ctx (arg storage must live in Ctx, not on the stack).
7. Per call: write the fresh caller pointers (x, w1, w2, g1, b1, g2, b2, out) into the Ctx arg storage and call cudaGraphExecKernelNodeSetParams only on the caller-pointer nodes (n_wt1, n_wt2, and t_k/ns_k/e_k for each chunk), then one cudaGraphLaunch on the current stream. `out = torch::empty_like(xc)` stays the only allocation; x is read-only (residual), no in-place mutation.
8. Fallback (identical results): if the caller stream is capturing, any graph API fails, or the cache is full, launch the same node sequence eagerly in chunk order.
9. Verify in nsys that conv_gemm of chunk k overlaps gstats/norm_silu/final_epilogue of chunk k-1, host launches per forward stay at 1, and max_atol <= 2.8e-3 on all four shapes.
